purpose: Simplify the measurement recipe and single notebook, while testing practical uniqueness of physical geometry.
operational_priority: Prefer fixed objective current. User confirms nonlinear image changes, history dependence, unknown coupled pre/post response and potentially changing aberrations. The earlier objective-sweep result is conditional on a response law that is not established experimentally.
requirements: One short notebook: acquire/simulate, analyse, fit, assess.
Reduce actual microscope operations where measured information permits; do not merely hide the old acquisition complexity.
Retain the physical-geometry objective and declare any remaining ambiguity.
Search varied physically valid starts; keep all acceptable distinct geometries and all failures.
Profile all four lens positions and thicknesses, source position, aperture axial position and both lateral coordinates; refit remaining unknowns from multiple starts.
Repeat the entire selected pixel/count experiment with independent noise, including image analysis; do not substitute noise added to fitted descriptors.
Introduce modest lens-response or calibration mismatch and assess geometry and prediction errors.
Assess all acceptable solutions against the accepted physical tolerances and prediction checks. Do not infer global uniqueness from local rank or frequency of convergence.
initial_simplification_candidates: Replace old aperture scans with one sweep through focus, initially testing one aperture diameter plus an open reference.
Reduce condenser settings and projector views, reanalysing selected pixels before claiming an acquisition reduction.
Keep objective current fixed where possible; quantify the remaining exact physical ambiguity and investigate an independent constraint rather than asserting it has disappeared.
Challenge the earlier objective-sweep fit with pre/post response mismatch and changing blur before treating that axis as useful experimentally.
status: Completed synthetic study: all four experiments pass practical geometry agreement, full individual profile-width tolerances, truth-error tolerances and frozen image/current predictions. The single notebook executed successfully.
